Create a Sankey diagram

Source: R/sankey_diagram.R
sankey_diagram.Rd

Draws flows between nodes as bands whose width is proportional to their value: each node is a bar as tall as the largest of what flows into it and out of it, and the nodes are laid out in columns from left to right. Use it for budgets, energy balances, user journeys or any process where quantities split and merge. The flows must not form a cycle.

Usage

sankey_diagram(
  data,
  source,
  target,
  value = NULL,
  colors = NULL,
  link_color = c("source", "target", "gradient", "grey"),
  align = c("justify", "left", "right", "center"),
  node_width = 14,
  node_padding = 12,
  link_opacity = 0.4,
  show_values = TRUE,
  value_format = ",.0f",
  label_font_size = 11,
  draggable = TRUE,
  hover = TRUE,
  animate = TRUE,
  title = NULL,
  title_font_size = 16,
  font = "Verdana, Geneva, Tahoma, sans-serif",
  bg_col = "white",
  text_col = "#333333",
  width = NULL,
  height = NULL
)

Arguments

data

A data frame with one row per flow.

source, target

The names of the columns giving the start and the end of each flow.

value

Optional. The name of a numeric column giving the size of each flow. When NULL, each row counts as 1. Rows with the same source and target are added up.

colors

Optional. Colours of the nodes: one per node (in order of appearance) or a named vector matched to the node names.

link_color

How to colour the flows: "source" (the default), "target", "gradient" (from the source colour to the target colour) or "grey".

align

How to place the nodes in columns: "justify" (the default; the end nodes go to the right edge), "left", "right" or "center".

node_width

The width of the nodes in pixels. Defaults to 14.

node_padding

The vertical gap between nodes in pixels. Defaults to 12.

link_opacity

The opacity of the flows. Defaults to 0.4.

show_values

Logical. Write the value of each node under its name. Defaults to TRUE.

value_format

A d3 format for the values. Defaults to ",.0f".

label_font_size

The font size of the node labels. Defaults to 11.

draggable

Logical. Let the viewer drag the nodes up and down. Defaults to TRUE.

hover

Logical. Show tooltips and highlight on hover. Defaults to TRUE.

animate

Logical. Let the flows run in when the chart is drawn. Defaults to TRUE.

title

Optional. The title of the chart.

title_font_size

The font size of the title. Defaults to 16.

font

The font family. Defaults to "Verdana, Geneva, Tahoma, sans-serif".

bg_col

The background colour. Defaults to "white".

text_col

The colour of the text. Defaults to "#333333".

width, height

Optional. The size of the chart.

Value

An r2d3 htmlwidget.

Interactions

Hover a flow to see its value and its share of the source and the target; hover a node to highlight everything that flows into it and out of it. Drag a node up or down to untangle the diagram (draggable). The flows run from left to right when the chart is drawn. Inside Shiny, clicking a node sets input$<id>_clicked to a list with node and value, and clicking a flow sets it to a list with source, target and value.

Examples

# A household budget
budget <- data.frame(
  from = c("Salary", "Salary", "Freelance", "Freelance", "Savings",
           "Savings", "Living", "Living", "Living"),
  to = c("Living", "Savings", "Living", "Savings", "Stocks",
         "Emergency fund", "Rent", "Food", "Transport"),
  amount = c(2600, 900, 500, 300, 700, 500, 1700, 900, 500)
)
sankey_diagram(budget, source = "from", target = "to", value = "amount",
               value_format = "$,.0f", title = "Where the money goes")



# Who survived the Titanic: class, then sex, then outcome
tt <- as.data.frame(Titanic)
tt$Survived <- ifelse(tt$Survived == "Yes", "Survived", "Died")
step1 <- aggregate(Freq ~ Class + Sex, data = tt, FUN = sum)
step2 <- aggregate(Freq ~ Sex + Survived, data = tt, FUN = sum)
names(step1) <- names(step2) <- c("from", "to", "people")
sankey_diagram(rbind(step1, step2), source = "from", target = "to",
               value = "people", link_color = "gradient",
               colors = c(Died = "#9498a0", Survived = "#3ca951"))
